description: Firsthand triage of every Slither finding that touches prototype/vnext-kernel/contracts (see the vNext Kernel PR description for the reachability argument behind each verdict). Keyed by "<check>|<sorted filename:line elements, de-duplicated across the per-entry-file recompilation crytic-compile's plain solc platform performs>" -- the same key generate-scanner-evidence.ts computes from a fresh --json run. generate-scanner-evidence.ts --validate fails if a fresh Slither run surfaces any finding whose key is not in this file, so an untriaged finding cannot silently disappear in a future change.

arbitrary-send-eth|prototype/vnext-kerne.rationale: egress(address) sends to migration.destinationVault, which is set exclusively by bindMigration (guardian quorum AND credential, see AUTHORITY.md section 3 "Migration takeover") and re-validated against migration.destinationVaultCodeHash at execution time. egress itself takes no destination parameter -- the detector's premise (an externally-influenced destination) does not hold.

execute's recipient is bound into the digest _authorise checks (HYBRID: ECDSA AND, when securityFloor.requirePq, the PQ verifier) before any value moves -- traced at VaultKernelPrototype.sol:605-613. The destination is exactly the parameter the signed authorization covers; this is a custody contract's spend function working as designed, not an unauthorized-destination bug.

assembly|prototype/vnext-kernel/contract.rationale: _attests's inline assembly is a bounded-gas (GUARDIAN_CALL_GAS), bounded-returndata (one word) STATICCALL that Solidity's high-level call syntax cannot express -- the whole point of I-GUARDIAN-FAULT-ISOLATION (AUTHORITY.md section 5/6). Removing it would remove the fault isolation, not just the assembly.

immutable-states|prototype/vnext-kernel/.rationale: ConfigurablePolicy is a test-only adversary/control fixture (PrototypeMocks.sol header: "None is measured by measure.ts"), never deployed as part of the measured kernel. Pure gas-optimization suggestion, no security content.
TestToken is a test-only fixture, never deployed as part of the measured kernel. Pure gas-optimization suggestion, no security content.

locked-ether|prototype/vnext-kernel/cont.rationale: DestinationStub is a test-only migration-destination stand-in ("a destination with code, so a migration binding has a real codehash", PrototypeMocks.sol comment); it exists only to give egress() tests a real codehash to check against, never to hold funds in production.

ReentrantRecipient is the test-only adversary that exercises AUTHORITY.md section 6's reentrancy argument ("a reentrant recipient cannot replay a spend, because the nonce is already consumed"). It is deliberately not meant to release funds.

low-level-calls|prototype/vnext-kernel/c.rationale: ReentrantRecipient.receive() re-entering the kernel is the mechanism of the M-K reentrancy test, not incidental.

egress's two low-level calls are exactly AUTHORITY.md section 5 call sites 4 and 6: empty-calldata value transfer to the bound destination, and a fixed-selector (0xa9059cbb) ERC-20 transfer to the same bound destination. Both destinations come from the committed migration binding, never from a per-call parameter.
execute's low-level call is AUTHORITY.md section 5 call site 4: empty calldata, value transfer only, to the signed-and-authorized recipient. Documented as deliberate ("never arbitrary execution").
_balanceOf's staticcall is AUTHORITY.md section 5 call site 6's balanceOf half: fixed selector 0x70a08231, read-only, used only to measure a settlement (I-NO-FALSE-SETTLEMENT).

missing-inheritance|prototype/vnext-kern.rationale: GasBurningGuardian's own doc comment states it is deliberately NOT declared IERC1271Guardian, because that interface is view and this adversary must be free to burn gas without a state-mutability restriction. Slither is correctly observing an intentional deviation.

missing-zero-check|prototype/vnext-kerne.rationale: RawCloner exists specifically to deploy a clone outside the factory's atomic init ("the M-K01 takeover window" per its own comment) -- it is the adversarial fixture, not code with a security property to enforce.
Same RawCloner adversarial fixture as the cloneOnly finding above.
ReentrantRecipient.arm is test-only wiring for the reentrancy adversary, not kernel code.

setPolicy's policy is documented and tested to accept address(0) on purpose: PLANE doc-comment states "address(0) falls back to the kernel FLOOR", and execute() at VaultKernelPrototype.sol:628-631 explicitly branches on policyEngine == address(0). A zero-check here would break the documented fallback behaviour, not fix a bug.

reentrancy-benign|prototype/vnext-kernel.rationale: This IS the AUTHORITY.md section 6 reentrancy adversary firing as designed -- the finding names the exact mechanism the suite tests.

reentrancy-events|prototype/vnext-kernel.rationale: deployVault's two external calls (cloneDeterministicWithImmutableArgs, then initialize) both target the clone address CREATE2 just produced in this same call -- a brand-new contract with no prior code cannot reenter deployVault before it exists. VaultDeployed is emitted after both calls with no state left for a reentrant call to exploit (the factory holds no mutable state at all -- VaultKernelFactoryPrototype.sol's own header: its authority closure is EMPTY).

egress is documented PERMISSIONLESS with NO discretion (AUTHORITY.md section 1/6): the recipient and asset disposition are fixed by the prior migration binding, so a reentrant call can only re-move balance to the same already-committed destination -- idempotent by construction, not an exploit path.

AUTHORITY.md section 6's documented argument, independently re-traced: _consume(DOMAIN_SPEND, ...) increments nonces[DOMAIN_SPEND] at VaultKernelPrototype.sol:614, strictly before the policy-plane call (628-631) and the value transfer (634). A reentrant execute() needs a fresh signature over nonce+1, which only the credential holder can produce -- reentry is authorized spending, not a bypass.

timestamp|prototype/vnext-kernel/contrac.rationale: executeRecovery checks block.timestamp against RECOVERY_DELAY (7 days) / RECOVERY_EXPIRY (14 days) windows. A miner's ~15s timestamp manipulation budget is immaterial at day-scale granularity and grants no capability the guardian quorum did not already grant by initiating recovery.
enterContainment's window/budget arithmetic (CONTAINMENT_WINDOW = 30 days, CONTAINMENT_BUDGET = 6 days) operates at day-scale; ~15s of miner timestamp slack cannot move the budget check's outcome.
retire() checks block.timestamp against BIND_DELAY (7 days). Day-scale window, immaterial to ~15s miner slack, and retire() carries no discretion regardless of exact timing.

egress's codehash re-check has no timestamp arithmetic in it that a miner could exploit; the timestamp read here is incidental to the surrounding function, not a comparison a miner can move a meaningful amount.

_requireIncomingPossession itself performs no timestamp comparison; the flagged lines are digest/signature checks reusing the enclosing function's timestamp-influenced call sites (rotateCredential / executeRecovery), already covered by those findings' own rationale.

_consume checks block.timestamp against a caller-supplied deadline. The deadline is the caller's own choice (like a normal transaction deadline pattern); ~15s of miner slack narrows or widens the window the caller themselves already accepted, and grants a miner no capability over WHO is authorized.

_effectiveState's CONTAINED-vs-NORMAL check compares against containedUntil, set from CONTAINMENT_MAX (3 days) in enterContainment. Day-scale window, immaterial to ~15s miner slack, and the effect of the ~15s ambiguity is which side of a state transition a call lands on that was already scheduled to happen -- not a new capability.

uninitialized-local|prototype/vnext-kern.rationale: egress's `moved` is assigned on every path: the if (asset == address(0)) branch assigns it directly, the else branch assigns it from before - remaining. Both branches of the if/else are exhaustive, so `moved` is never read before assignment despite lacking an explicit literal initializer.

_requireQuorum's `counted` is a uint256 local, which Solidity zero-initializes deterministically (not an uninitialized-storage-pointer aliasing hazard, the genuinely dangerous case this detector exists for). The loop only ever increments it from that known-zero start.

unused-return|prototype/vnext-kernel/con.rationale: EcdsaBackedVerifier.verify destructures ECDSA.tryRecover's THREE return values as (recovered, err, ), using both recovered and err in the following return statement; only the third value (unused by the OZ ECDSA API for this check) is intentionally discarded via the idiomatic blank identifier. Test-only fixture besides.

_attests destructures ECDSA.tryRecover the same way and uses both recovered and err in `return err == ECDSA.RecoverError.NoError && recovered == guardian && recovered != address(0);` -- the blanked third value is intentionally discarded, standard Solidity idiom, not an ignored result.
